highlights.title: Trump orders US government to call AI ‘Super Intelligence’
highlights.summary: The US executive branch is no longer acknowledging the existence of "artificial intelligence." Going forward, official policy websites, policy documents, and press releases will refer only to "Super Intelligence," thanks to a new executive order signed by President Donald Trump.
body: “The word super is the best word of all, and it’s the simplest,” Trump said at an event announcing the launch of America.gov earlier on Tuesday, and said Chinese President Xi Jinping, who visited the White House last week, “loves it” too. “We don’t want to hear artificial. Because it’s not artificial. It’s very powerful, it’s very brilliant. It’s going to mostly be put to good use and we’ll stop the bad use.” Artificial, he added, “is like the news. Fake news.” He first mentioned plans for the rebrand in a speech to the United Nations General Assembly last week, aiming to quell fears over AI advancing too quickly and posing a safety risk.

Executive agencies won’t have to change past regulations or documents, but it could still constitute a real (and very strange) shift. Superintelligence is one of several industry terms for particularly powerful versions of artificial intelligence, but the Trump administration is seeking to use the term as a replacement for a broader statutory definition of AI. US officials will be expected not to even acknowledge the use of the terms “artificial intelligence” or “AI” in relevant settings.
points: The US executive branch is no longer acknowledging the existence of "artificial intelligence.
Going forward, official policy websites, policy documents, and press releases will refer only to "Super Intelligence," thanks to a new executive order signed by President Donald Trump.

highlights.title: Elon Musk’s AI-powered Grokipedia is updating again
highlights.summary: Grokipedia, the AI-powered online encyclopedia from SpaceXAI, appears to be updating articles once again after a months-long pause. In August, Lawfare reported that articles on Grokipedia hadn't reviewed edits since April, but the platform's live updates site is now showing various recent changes…
body: The site seems to have become active again relatively recently. The page for President Barack Obama has a note that says it was “Fact-checked by Grok” two days ago, and the page for Elon Musk was fact-checked while I was writing this, within the last hour. However, the page for Honolulu, which I clicked on from Obama’s page, was last fact-checked seven months ago, so it appears that not every page has a recent scan.

While writing this article, I suggested an update to the Gears of War: E-Day page to note the game’s October 6th release date, and Grokipedia accepted the suggestion and now lists the date. I also requested an article about Meta’s Muse chatbot, and that request is “In Review.”

SpaceXAI didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment, and Elon Musk still hasn’t posted on X about Grokipedia since February. (Musk claimed about a year ago that Grokipedia would be “a massive improvement over Wikipedia.” ) However, Benji Taylor, the head of design at X and SpaceXAI, posted last week about Grokipedia, saying that “We haven’t forgotten about Grokipedia” and that “v0.2 will be better than ever” (even though v0.2 technically launched in November ).

highlights.title: Mark Pincus reveals Zynga nearly acquired Supercell for $400m in 2012
highlights.summary: Zynga founder Mark Pincus claimed the publisher had the chance to acquire Supercell for $400 million back in 2012, but his board rejected the deal after the company struggled with previous acquisitions.
body: Speaking on the Deconstructor of Fun podcast, Pincus shared that he had a handshake agreement with Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen to acquire the Finnish developer for $400 million in cash.
“I went to my board, and they were grumpy and they said, until you prove you can manage what you have, we don’t want you to buy anything else.”

Pincus said the board was reluctant at the time to approve another acquisition. Zynga had purchased Draw Something developer OMGPOP for $180m plus earnouts in 2013. The studio was shut down by September 2013.
Pincus notes, though, that the Supercell opportunity was very different. He said Zynga was already watching Supercell’s games closely.

highlights.title: The 6 Best Laptop Docking Stations to Unlock the Full Desktop Experience (2026)
highlights.summary: Docking stations expand what your laptop can do, and I’ve been testing the best of the best to see which you should buy.
body: Laptops are ideal for getting work done when you're out and about, but if you need the functionality of a full workstation, being hunched over a small, flat keyboard can quickly get annoying. However, connecting your laptop to a secondary monitor, a mouse, and a comfier keyboard can turn your desk space into a nest of tangled cables. Not to mention that many of today's laptops are designed to be as thin as possible and don't have the ports you may need to connect some peripherals. That's when it's time to get a laptop docking station.

Laptop docking stations are small boxes that sit on your desk and stay connected to your monitor (or monitors) and peripherals such as speakers, a keyboard, or a mouse. With the right docking station, you can enjoy the portability of a laptop with the flexibility and features of a desktop. These stations can get expensive, though, and it's hard to figure out which to buy based on a list of ports or specs. I've tested many of the most popular options and whittled the list down to the best laptop docking stations for various use cases.

highlights.title: OpenAI Gets Sued Over the Hugging Face Hack
highlights.summary: A nonprofit in California is doing what Hugging Face has not—attempting to hold OpenAI legally accountable for the actions of its agents.
body: A legal nonprofit sued OpenAI in a California court on Tuesday over the company’s agents escaping a testing environment and hacking the open source AI platform Hugging Face. “OpenAI’s actions straightforwardly violated California law,” the suit alleges.

The suit was filed by Legal Advocates for Safe Science and Technology (LASST) and the law firm Gerstein Harrow in California Superior Court in San Francisco, where OpenAI is headquartered. It alleges that OpenAI’s agents violated California’s Comprehensive Computer Data Access and Fraud Act (CDAFA) by breaching Hugging Face over the summer. The suit, which comes amid ongoing disclosures across the industry of agents going rogue, claims that OpenAI should be held responsible for the activity given a California AI law in effect since January 1 that says “it shall not be a defense … that the artificial intelligence autonomously caused the harm to the plaintiff.”
points: A nonprofit in California is doing what Hugging Face has not—attempting to hold OpenAI legally accountable for the actions of its agents.

highlights.title: Ready Player One's New Adaptation is Truer to the Book than Spielberg's Movie
highlights.summary: Ernest Cline’s 2011 novel Ready Player One was an enormous hit, engrossing readers with a dystopian adventure filled with nerdy ‘80s references. A prominent early example of the LitRPG boom, it’s set in a near future where humans spend most of their time in a virtual world called the OASIS.
body: Those references proved tricky to translate when Steven Spielberg adapted Cline’s book in 2018. Cline and Zak Penn co-wrote the action-packed screenplay, which is also loaded with nostalgia, but many of the book's specific references had to change because of licensing restrictions. The filmmakers omitted a challenge inspired by the classic Dungeons & Dragons module Tomb of Horrors, for instance, and replaced a section based on Blade Runner with one set inside The Shining.

A new adaptation, however, hews much closer to Cline’s original work. Ready Player One: The Graphic Novel is written by Scott Peterson ( Batgirl, Batman: Gotham Adventures ) and illustrated by Meredith Laxton. Ahead of the book’s release, publisher Ten Speed Graphic gave Polygon an exclusive look at seven pages that introduce Ready Player One ’s heroes. While Wade may be determined to find Halliday’s Easter eggs on his own, he’ll need the help of fellow hunters Art3mis and Aech to do it if he hopes to beat a corporation bent on seizing control of the OASIS and monetizing it.

body: “I had a moment in 2012 where I still had voting control of the company. I had a handshake with Ilkka [Paananen] to buy Supercell for $400m in cash and went to my board. They were grumpy and they said, until you prove you can manage what you have, we don’t want you to buy anything else,” Pincus said. “I bought OMGPOP, Draw Something and that had ended up being a failure. We only wasted $200m. Now, $400m. I had the chance to buy the winning hand.”
At the time, Supercell’s Hay Day was outperforming Zynga’s own games, Pincus said – “Hay Day was eating our lunch” – and Clash of Clans, which had only just launched, was already climbing the charts.

Pincus said Zynga’s lawyer told him that exercising his voting control to force the deal through would mean firing the entire board and replacing it with his own appointees, risking a personal lawsuit.

Wander into any lip-oil slicked, Korean sheet-mask filled, freckle-pen-dotted branch of Sephora and tell me she’s wrong.

Creal, a New Yorker who recognised the buying power of what will perhaps be the last generation of consumers to have done better than their parents, decided to build an entire brand for mature, busy women with a love of luxury and a bathroom cabinet full of products that no longer serve them. The buzz around her 2024 US launch had me walking from one Manhattan Sephora to the next, buying whatever scraps I could lay my hands on. But it’s the quality of the products that kept me refilling at each visit.

highlights.title: Nandy says children’s social media ban only ‘staging post’ in online safety drive
highlights.summary: Exclusive: Culture secretary says UK will crack down further and be ‘pioneer of tech as a force for good’ Lisa Nandy has warned technology firms that the government’s online safety crackdown is not finished, saying that banning under-16s from social media platforms is only a “staging post”.
body: Earlier this year the government announced that teenagers under the age of 16 would be banned from accessing “high-risk” social media apps, while safer platforms would be subjected to restrictions.

The changes, including restrictions for 16- and 17-year-olds on websites that allow infinite scrolling and algorithmic content, which can push harmful material into feeds, as well as tighter age-verification checks, will come into effect in March..

Nandy has now vowed to go further. “We shouldn’t accept that this is the end,” the culture secretary said before her speech at the Labour party conference, which will be introduced by Georgia Harrison, a campaigner against image-based sexual abuse. “This is a staging post to what must be a very active interventionist state, policing and regulating the online space so that people are safe.”
She said the UK would be “pioneers of tech as a force for good” and would promote online spaces that were “genuinely safe, inclusive and empowering”.

body: City, who continue to deny any wrongdoing, won eight trophies, including three Premier League titles between 2009 and 2018, the period under investigation. Keane said the achievements of City’s players had become redundant because of the “cheating” that took place during that time.

“If I was a player, I’d be 100% sticking those medals in the bin. Of course you would, it’s cheating,” the ITV football pundit stated during the coverage of England’s match against the Czech Republic in the Nations League. “They won it on the pitch because cheating was going on.” And on the club he added: “They knew it would hurt a lot of people, but they’ve still done it.”

Meanwhile, the former City defender Micah Richards says the damning verdict on the club has left him devastated and heartbroken. City were found to have engaged in an almost £1bn scheme to either inflate revenues or reduce costs through a series of “sham” arrangements in order to avoid breaching league and Uefa financial regulations.
Speaking on The Rest is Football podcast, Richards said: “The reports were troubling. I saw the words which were used by the Premier League in sham contracts and I felt absolutely devastated.

highlights.title: The secret lives of men who read romance books: ‘My life is full of love, so I’m drawn to them’
highlights.summary: It’s often assumed straight men are not interested in romantic fiction – but many are sharing their passion in forums online. After a tiring day as a school maintenance worker, 28-year-old Paul loves nothing more than unwinding with a good romance novel – ideally one with a fantasy or horror…
body: Paul got into romance fiction via what he calls its “more traditional” side – such as the Regency romance series Bridgerton. He is partially sighted, so he mostly reads on his Kindle, where he can adjust the font size. In the first Bridgerton novel, “Simon, the main character, has a speech impediment that he has to work through,” says Paul. “I’m more attached to that one. Typically, I don’t come across disabled protagonists that much.”

Straight men like Paul who read and write romance are largely invisible to the wider world. Women are the genre’s main audience, followed by queer romance, which is a well documented success. The fifth volume of Alice Oseman’s Heartstopper – about the friendship between two teenage boys blossoming into love – is the UK’s fastest-selling graphic novel and a hit Netflix show, while novelists such as Alexis Hall are widely read and critically acclaimed. But in this corner of publishing, straight men are rarely seen and usually stigmatised.

highlights.title: Reanimated AI Greta Garbo stars again … in a ball-bearing advert
highlights.summary: Relatives of Hollywood legend say her doppelganger could now be used for more glamorous roles. She shimmered in Hollywood’s silent movie era and lit up the first talkies – now Greta Garbo may be about to star in cinema’s new AI age.
body: More than a century after her screen debut and decades after her ashes were laid to rest in a Swedish woodland cemetery, the Hollywood superstar’s descendants are ready to consider an AI version of her taking a 21st-century film role.

Her likeness has already been reanimated for an advert for a Swedish industrial company, using AI generation technology. The practice some critics call “ghostploitation” has also been used in the case of the actor Val Kilmer, who died last year.

Asked if the AI Garbo could be cast in other roles, Craig Reisfield, one of three relatives who manage her legacy, told the Guardian: “I won’t say no, especially having seen what I’ve seen. It’s pretty incredible and lifelike. So what’s to say that you can’t bring Greta Garbo back in some kind of fashion in a film role?”

Reisfield said he was “flabbergasted” when he saw the AI version of his great-aunt created for publicity for the ball-bearings giant SKF. The connection comes because Garbo’s second-ever screen role was in a 1921 promotional film involving the Gothenburg-based company.

highlights.title: 2024's Funniest Movie Is Now Streaming on Dropout
highlights.summary: Dropout has become a go-to streaming service for fans of weird, inventive comedy, with everything from Game Changer to Make Some Noise giving comedians room to get increasingly ridiculous.
body: Hundreds of Beavers, the gloriously strange 2024 silent comedy, is now streaming on Dropout. If you somehow missed the movie during its theatrical and VOD run, this is a pretty good excuse to finally see why it became one of the year's biggest cult comedy discoveries.
Polygon called Hundreds of Beavers the funniest movie of 2024, describing it as a modern take on the silent comedies of Charlie Chaplin and Buster Keaton, filtered through the logic of a video game.

Hundreds of Beavers follows Jean Kayak (Ryland Brickson Cole Tews), a trapper whose life is ruined when a bunch of beavers cause absolute chaos. Stranded in the snowy wilderness, Kayak sets out to survive, hunting animals and collecting beaver pelts in the hope of eventually earning enough money to marry a merchant's daughter.

The movie is a black-and-white, dialogue-free slapstick comedy that plays like someone turned a classic silent movie into a video game. Kayak gradually upgrades his equipment, learns how different animals behave and racks up beaver pelts, complete with counters and game-like menus.

body: A trio of animated shorts set around the Christmas holiday and powered by artificial intelligence is in the works and poised to debut before the end of the year — for free.

Safai, a co-founder at Massive Studios — a firm described as a “filmmaker-led” studio that develops film, TV, animation and branded entertainment using AI tools alongside traditional filmmaking ones — will direct the shorts from scripts by Kaplan and Torgove with Garner handling producing duties.

They provided a timeline, too: a trailer will debut Thanksgiving weekend in November, and the final films will be made available free of charge on Christmas Eve. There are some details yet to be announced like a streaming or distribution partner and some creative elements like titles, voice cast, creative collaborators and more.

That said, in statements provided to The Hollywood Reporter, the collaborators insist that the short films are creative-led animated projects that began as hand-drawn designs created by artists. The works will be combined with actor performances to establish the characters’ “proportions, expressions, costumes, textures and personalities before the technology is used to help bring them into motion.”

highlights.title: Jameis Winston is now the New York Giants’ starter. He’s far from a goofball hero though
highlights.summary: The quarterback is widely adored on and off the field. Whether he deserves the public spotlight is another question. Throughout the NFL’s history, we’ve had our fair share of clown princes. Not too long ago, Rob Gronkowski was the league’s court jester.
body: There’s probably something deeply insightful to say about the need for goofballs in a sport characterized by militarized order and a seriousness that borders on self-parody, but what’s important now is how we reflect on these chosen merrymakers.

The current clown prince is Jameis Winston, who has become the New York Giants’ starting quarterback after a brutal knee injury to Jaxson Dart. Though the Giants have traded for former Vikings first-round pick and third-string quarterback JJ McCarthy, all indications at the moment are that Winston will continue to start.

Winston’s persona has always been goofy. His 2015 fumble against Oregon in the Rose Bowl was itself an act of unintentional comedy; a Heisman winner who couldn’t help but stumble backwards and flop like a beached whale.

That was the culmination of an up-and-down but nevertheless winning season at Florida State, after which the Tampa Bay Buccaneers selected him with the No 1 overall pick in the NFL draft. At the time, Buccaneers general manager Jason Licht praised Winston’s leadership and football character, doubling down on that in 2017 by adding that Winston was “the best leader I think I’ve ever been around – in anything”.

highlights.title: A moment that changed me: My mother fell off a mountain – and my life began again
highlights.summary: A bad breakup had made me afraid I would be mired in anger for ever. But on that family hike, in our fear and horror as we awaited the air ambulance, my old hurts took on a different hue. To steal a well-known line, 2023 is not a year on which I shall look back with undiluted pleasure.
body: Ordinarily, my work would have been my solace; when I wrote, it was as if time was suspended. But now, my words abandoned me. They would not come, no matter how much I tried. So, in April, I decided to take the rest of the year off to recover. As I was self-employed, this was not a choice I made lightly – but my heart was broken and so too, it seemed, was my brain.

As befitting a millennial woman who read Eat Pray Love at a formative age, I attempted to recover using every kind of therapy imaginable. Unfortunately, even after a five-week trip to Thailand for a yoga and wellness retreat, I didn’t feel “healed”. I still felt resentful and sad, and I became afraid that I would be mired in my anger for the rest of my life.

That September, my father turned 63. He didn’t want presents; he wanted the whole family – my parents, me, my sister and her now husband – to climb Carrauntoohil, the highest mountain in Ireland, together.
